bull_bear.body:
- Differentiated capabilities across financial services, healthcare, retail and data-intensive industries built through web and mobile application development, big data platforms, data engineering and analytics
- Internally developed software platform being amortised and productised, described by management as a strategic asset in the Company's long-term IP portfolio
- Depth in data engineering and analytics which management believes positions it to address enterprise demand for AI-ready infrastructure and intelligent data pipelines
- Experienced workforce and established client relationships
- RBI lifting restrictions on banking partnerships enables Saven to collaborate with more financial institutions on co-branded credit card programs
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US offshore client base exposed to tariff wars and trade tensions — Management states the offshore business outlook, particularly in the United States, has become more volatile; escalating tariff wars and trade-related tensions could disrupt existing offshore contracts and future opportunities, and as U.S. firms recalibrate global sourcing strategies Saven may face headwinds in maintaining and growing its offshore client base.
- AI-powered development tools disrupting traditional IT service consumption — Management acknowledges that rapid enterprise adoption of AI-powered development tools is beginning to impact traditional IT service consumption models, pressuring the conventional offshore delivery model the Company's Offshore Development & Services business rests on.
- Client internalisation of technology functions and shifting client priorities — Increasing internalisation of technology functions by clients, alongside shifting client priorities, is described as posing ongoing challenges to conventional offshore delivery — a structural threat to outsourced demand.
- High entry barriers and intense competition in the AI domain — The AI pivot the Company is making carries high entry barriers, significant upfront investments and fierce competition from both large tech players and agile startups; the Company is mitigating through workforce upskilling and agile solution delivery.
- Evolving RBI regulation of the Indian fintech opportunity — The Indian fintech landscape remains complex due to evolving RBI guidelines on data privacy, cybersecurity and fraud prevention, requiring the Company to continuously adapt its offerings to remain compliant without compromising innovation — a compliance burden on the fintech growth plank.
- Cautious enterprise technology spending and macroeconomic headwinds — Management cites inflationary pressures, cautious technology spending, signs of moderation in the US economy, cautious enterprise spending in key international markets and geopolitical tensions from the ongoing Middle East conflict as near-term challenges weighing on the industry.
- Competition for specialised talent and dependence on continuous reskilling — The industry must navigate intense competition for specialised talent and rapid technological obsolescence; the Company's response is workforce reskilling and AI talent development, making execution on skills a dependency for its stated strategy.
- Industry-level pricing pressure and technology spending cycles — Management notes the industry will need to navigate global technology spending cycles, pricing pressures and evolving data, AI and cybersecurity regulations — structural margin and demand risks for a small specialised provider.

outlook.body:
- Securing engagements in artificial intelligence and data engineering, both in the US market and domestically in India, with new client acquisition in these emerging verticals named the primary management objective for the current year
- Positioning in AI application development by investing in AI talent development and building solution prototypes that embed AI into customers' existing tools and platforms
- Workforce reskilling and alignment of service offerings with AI-augmented delivery in response to structural pressure on conventional offshore delivery
- Expanding in Indian fintech, using the RBI's lifting of restrictions on banking partnerships to collaborate with more financial institutions on co-branded credit card programs aimed at small and medium-sized businesses
- Rebuilding the BPO vertical through targeted additions after prior-year rationalisation, with a new engagement commenced during the current year
- Productising and amortising the internally developed software platform as a strategic asset in the Company's long-term IP portfolio
- Prioritising workforce upskilling and agile solution delivery to offset high entry barriers and competition in the AI domain
- Maintaining operational discipline and pursuing disciplined, quality-led growth
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections do not set out a capex or capacity-expansion programme. Expansion is described only as market/footprint intent: management calls India a high-potential market for Saven's strategic expansion in fintech, citing the RBI's lifting of restrictions on banking partnerships as enabling collaboration with more financial institutions to launch co-branded credit card programs. No project names, commissioning timelines, delivery-centre additions or rupee capex quantum are disclosed in this text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management believes underlying demand for technology services remains resilient over the medium to long term despite macroeconomic headwinds, as enterprises continue to prioritise digital modernisation, process automation and analytics-driven decision-making
- Demand for AI application development is described as resilient, with businesses across industries accelerating digital transformation and driving demand for AI-powered solutions
- Management believes the Company's depth in data engineering and analytics positions it well to address growing enterprise demand for AI-ready infrastructure and intelligent data pipelines
- The fintech sector in India is said to offer immense growth opportunities, supported by a large digitally engaged population, rising smartphone penetration and government financial-inclusion initiatives; the RBI banking-partnership relaxation is expected to open a significant revenue stream
- The offshore business outlook, particularly in the United States, has become more volatile; tariff wars and trade tensions could disrupt existing offshore contracts and future opportunities as U.S. firms recalibrate global sourcing
- Near-term challenges flagged: geopolitical tensions from the ongoing Middle East conflict, signs of moderation in the US economy, and cautious enterprise spending in key international markets
- Structural pressure on the global outsourcing environment from rapid enterprise adoption of AI-powered development tools, increasing internalisation of technology functions and shifting client priorities
- Inflationary pressures and cautious technology spending continue to weigh on the industry
- Industry context cited: global IT spending estimated at around USD 5.6 trillion in 2025 and expected at approximately USD 6.4 trillion in CY 2026; Indian IT industry revenues estimated at approximately USD 315 billion in FY 2025-26 versus around USD 297 billion in the preceding year
